To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a microfluidic platform for magnetic particle manipulation has been developed, which allows the detection and characterization of single magnetic microparticles with diameters between 1 and 30 μm.
the combination of magnetic actuation and single-photon detection allows for a highly sensitive detection of magnetic microparticles in microfluidic systems.

a hybrid CMOS microsystem that combines magnetic actuator with in situ optical particle detection was developed and that single microparticles could be transported, detected and evaluated with high sensitivity and accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a CMOS-based microsystem for the detection and manipulation of magnetic particles in a microfluidic environment.
the development of a CMOS-based microsystem that combines magnetic actuated transport of microparticles and single photon detection in a single microfluidic device.

the development of a microfluidic system, where the actuation of magnetic microparticles is performed using a magnetic field and the detection of the particles is performed optically using a single photon detector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented system is able to perform magnetic manipulation and optical detection in a single device.
we have developed and demonstrated a novel hybrid microfluidic system for the magnetic actuation and single-particle optical detection of magnetic microparticles.
the presented system is capable to handle and detect single magnetic particles in the μm range and to evaluate their size and magnetic properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and tested a new microfluidic system, that combines magnetic actuating and optical detection.
we present a novel CMOS-based microsystem that combines magnetic actuated transport of particles with a highly sensitive detection of particles using SPADs.
the presented microfluidic system allows the detection and evaluation of individual microparticles with diameters ranging down to 1 μm and with a detection sensitivity of 0.1 μm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of magnetic actuation and optical detection in a CMOS system enables the development of a versatile microsystem for the manipulation and characterization of microparticles.
a hybrid microsystem combining magnetic microparticle actuation and in-situ photometry can be realized in a CMOS process.
a hybrid CMOS microsystem that combines magnetic actuations and in situ optical sensing can be used for a fast and reliable determination of microparticles properties.
